gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EPICKA's own listing says the Pulse Duo 65W's AC outlet accepts 13 of the 15 plug types (Types A–O), against 10 for the TA-105 Max, while both slide-out plugs skip Type D and Type M sockets.
standout_why: I compared against Kit Authority (cited in 2 chats), TrekSavvy and MobilePlusTech, and I tried WIRED, which is cited but blocked fetching. Kit Authority already names the Type D (India) and Type M (South Africa) exclusions for TESSAN and EPICKA. It also lists which plugs fit the TA-105's AC outlet and gives the TA-105 Max port splits. TrekSavvy already gives the Air 65W's drop to 40 W + 15 W and the Air's D/M exclusion. None of these pages gives an accepted-plug count for the Pulse Duo or the Air, and none says that full 65 W needs a cable rated above 3 A. Because Kit Authority and TrekSavvy cover the exclusions, the new finding is a refinement, not a fact that decides the pick.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. Every candidate (TESSAN WTA07/WTA09, EPICKA Air 65W, Pulse Duo 65W) uses the same A/C/G/I plug set and none fits D or M sockets, so country coverage can't separate them. Below 65 W the candidates differ in two ways. The first is how much the laptop port drops when a phone is plugged in: TrekSavvy reports 40 W + 15 W on the Air, and EPICKA's Air listing claims PD stays at 20 W during multi-port use. The second is how many foreign plugs the AC outlet takes: 13 of 15 on the Pulse Duo, per EPICKA. The Pulse Duo is $49.99 at EPICKA, which is still under $50. The TA-105 Max is out at $59.99.
